features.git.commit.what: Who runs git commit in your code repo. agent commits after you confirm. user stages the change and prints the message, and you take it from there.
features.git.commit.when: you want to keep your hands on every commit.

features.git.push.what: Whether the agent pushes. false commits locally only.
features.git.push.when: the repo has no remote yet, or you push by hand.

features.git.pr.what: How a pull request is opened: as a draft, ready for review, or not at all.
features.git.pr.when: you work alone (never) or your team reviews straight away (ready).

features.git.branchPrefix.what: A prefix for branches the loop creates, such as feat/. Left unset, it follows the repo's own convention.
features.git.branchPrefix.when: your team has a naming rule the repo does not show.

features.git.worktree.what: Does each workstream's code changes in its own git worktree, so your main checkout stays untouched.
features.git.worktree.when: you run several sessions on one repo.

features.postPush.watchCI.what: Watches CI after a push through the host's own CLI and fixes what goes red. It checks for a merge conflict first, because a conflict stops CI from running at all.
features.postPush.watchCI.when: the repo has CI and the host CLI is signed in.

features.postPush.finalHeadedTest.what: Runs one last drive of the changed screens in a visible browser, once CI is green.
features.postPush.finalHeadedTest.when: you want a final look at the real thing before merging.

features.postPush.flakePatterns.what: Patterns for failures you know to be flaky. A match is labelled as a known flake and the rerun command is suggested. Nothing is rerun by itself, and an unmatched failure still counts as a real one.
features.postPush.flakePatterns.when: one CI job fails at random and wastes your time.

platform.host.what: Where the code is hosted, which decides the CLI used for pull requests. auto reads it from the repo's origin remote.
platform.host.when: the remote's address does not show the host, such as a self-hosted server.

platform.tracker.what: The issue tracker your ticket ids come from. none leaves ids as plain text.
platform.tracker.when: your branch or initiative names carry ids like ABC-123.

platform.ticketPattern.what: A regular expression for your ticket ids, such as ACME-\d+.
platform.ticketPattern.when: your ids do not look like ABC-123.

platform.ticketUrl.what: The address of a ticket, with {id} where the id goes.
platform.ticketUrl.when: you set a tracker and want ids turned into links.

verification.what: How the agent drives a change itself. browser uses a real browser, api calls a live server, mobile uses a device or emulator, generic runs the real command. auto picks from the project type.
verification.when: the type of a project does not match how it is really used.

features.selfTest.unhappyPaths.what: Which failure paths the self-test must force besides the happy path.
features.selfTest.unhappyPaths.when: a path does not exist on a surface, such as no loading state.

features.selfTest.maxIterations.what: How many fix-and-retry rounds the self-test gets before it reports the result as flaky instead of guessing.
features.selfTest.maxIterations.when: a slow project burns too much on retries.

features.selfTest.smokePass.what: Adds a short drive over the app's core flows, not only the screens that changed.
features.selfTest.smokePass.when: changes tend to break things far from where they were made.

features.selfTest.record.what: Records the browser self-test as evidence: video, trace, both, or only when something goes wrong. Needs a Playwright MCP server started with --caps=devtools.
features.selfTest.record.when: you want proof of a drive to attach to a review.

tests.unit.what: Whether the loop writes unit tests. false writes no new ones, and the existing suite still runs.
tests.unit.when: a project has no unit test setup and should not get one.

testHooks.what: The attribute the self-test finds elements by, such as data-testid.
testHooks.when: the project uses something other than what the scan found.

features.browserDriver.what: What drives the browser self-test. auto uses the Playwright MCP server when connected. claude-chrome is for Claude Code only, with the Claude in Chrome extension.
features.browserDriver.when: you need your real, signed-in Chrome.

features.browserMode.what: Whether Playwright shows a window. Set when the server starts, so a session cannot change it midway. The loop looks for an MCP server named playwright for headed runs and playwright-headless for headless ones.
features.browserMode.when: you run on a server or want to keep working undisturbed.

features.screenshots.mode.what: When pull request screenshots are taken. auto takes them only if a change alters something visible.
features.screenshots.mode.when: you want them always, or never.

features.screenshots.viewports.what: Which sizes to capture: desktop, tablet, mobile.
features.screenshots.viewports.when: the project has a phone layout worth showing.

features.screenshots.darkMode.what: Also captures each shot in the dark colour scheme.
features.screenshots.darkMode.when: the app has a dark mode.

rules.what: A path to a Markdown file of hard rules for this project, which the loop must honour.
rules.when: something must always hold, such as "no new dependencies".

review.reportFormat.what: A path to your own template for the review report.
review.reportFormat.when: your team expects a set format.

groups.title: Model tiers and escalation
groups.intro: The stage table is under Models below.

orchestration.tiers.cheap.what: The real model behind the cheap tier. Unset, your agent decides.
orchestration.tiers.cheap.when: you want a specific model for routine stages.

orchestration.tiers.standard.what: The real model behind the standard tier.

orchestration.tiers.strong.what: The real model behind the strong tier.

orchestration.escalation.enabled.what: Moves a stalled stage up to a stronger model instead of retrying on the same one.
orchestration.escalation.enabled.when: you need a hard ceiling on cost.

orchestration.escalation.to.model.what: The tier a stalled stage moves up to.

orchestration.escalation.to.effort.what: The effort it runs at there.

orchestration.escalation.to.isolate.what: Whether the escalated stage runs in its own subagent.

stages.orient: Reading the state of the work
